newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS pledges to remain universal bank.
newsitem.headline: UBS pledges to remain universal bank.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) renewed its pledge on Thursday to remain a universal bank rather than narrowing its focus to investment banking or its lucrative business in asset management.
But chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta told shareholders UBS still planned to expand its asset management side and believed an acquisition was likely.
"We are still committed to being a bank," Cabiallavetta told the annual shareholder meeting.
"This means that we want to be neither a pure investment bank, nor a pure asset management company," he added.

Shareholder activist and Swiss financier Martin Ebner, whose BZ Bank is the biggest investor in UBS through its investment funds, has pressed UBS for years to shed its less profitable businesses and become exclusively an asset manager in order to boost shareholder value.
UBS' new structure since the start of the year includes private banking and institutional asset management, trading, international and domestic corporate finance and Swiss retail business.
Cabiallavetta noted that asset management was the strongest earnings driver.
"Particularly in our activities outside Switzerland, we believe a further expansion will bring significant benefits, and there is some likelihood that we will do this via acquisition," he said.
Cabiallavetta has said several times this years that UBS is interested in a U.S. acquisition in order to establish a significant presence in the world's biggest asset management market.
Cabiallavetta also repeated the strategic goal of turning loss-making Swiss retail banking into a profitable business.
"Our goal is to achieve a leading and profitable position in the Swiss market through a high level of service quality and innovative products," he told shareholders. -- Zurich Newsroom +41-1-631 7340
